title: After-hours parent messages compete with family time
brite: T · Assertive communication and boundaries; R · Parent communication
resources: Personal: assertiveness. Contextual: agreed response window and urgent channel.
teacher_move: Use a standard reply: Thank you for your message. I check this channel on school days and will reply during the next school day.
school_move: Agree on response hours and a staffed route for urgent matters. Share the policy with families.
check: Count evenings interrupted over one week.

title: Repeated forms, grading, reporting, Dapodik and routine meetings
resources: Personal: prioritization. Contextual: shared templates and authority to simplify workflow.
teacher_move: Map one repeated workflow. Mark required reporting and places where the same data is entered twice.
school_move: Assign one owner and one approved source for a recurring report. Trial replacing one routine meeting with a written update.
check: Compare minutes spent before and after the trial.

title: Event committees, extracurriculars and homeroom supervision crowd out core work
brite: T · Setting boundaries; i · Work–life balance
resources: Personal: negotiation. Contextual: duty rota and leadership discretion.
teacher_move: Ask: If I take on this event, which existing duty should move or be shared? Bring a one-week duty snapshot.
school_move: Publish a rotation, plan coverage, and swap or remove a duty when assigning an extra one.
check: Track whether protected prep time actually happened.

title: Setting limits can invite judgment, especially when leadership support feels weak
brite: R · Support networks; T · Assertive communication
resources: Personal: clear communication. Contextual: trusted peer and safe route for concerns.
teacher_move: Rehearse a neutral request with a colleague. If direct discussion feels unsafe, ask the appropriate trusted representative about confidential options.
school_move: Provide a confidential way to raise recurring workload concerns and report back on decisions.
check: Name the person who can act on the request and set a follow-up date.

title: Teaching while stressed and pressure to look composed or perfect
brite: E · Emotional awareness and classroom climate
resources: Personal: noticing cues and repairing mistakes. Contextual: peer backup and predictable routines.
teacher_move: Notice your first stress cue. Give a familiar quiet starter while you reset. If you spoke sharply, acknowledge it and restate the instruction calmly.
school_move: Agree on a discreet buddy signal and coverage plan when a teacher needs a brief handover.
check: Check whether the class could restart and whether the teacher had a chance to recover.

title: Burnout timing, signs and what to do when teaching continues daily
brite: B · Resilience process; i · Responding to stress
resources: Personal: recognizing a pattern. Contextual: coverage, workload adjustment and access to professional support.
teacher_move: There is no fixed year. Watch for ongoing exhaustion, detachment or cynicism about work, and reduced sense of effectiveness. For tomorrow, reuse a familiar lesson and ask for specific coverage. Seek professional support if distress persists or interferes with daily functioning.
school_move: Agree which duties to pause or reassign and review the adjustment in one week.
check: Check whether workload actually fell and recovery time increased.

title: Supporting students and colleagues without taking on every concern
brite: R · Teamwork; T · Help-seeking and boundaries
resources: Personal: listening and role clarity. Contextual: referral routes and regular peer consultation.
teacher_move: Ask: Would you like me to listen, brainstorm, or help find the right person? Agree on one next step and who owns it.
school_move: Clarify teacher, counselor and leadership roles. Protect time for consultation and establish a handover route.
check: Check that every handover has an agreed owner.

title: Large classes, diverse needs and questions about noticing student stress
brite: E · Classroom emotional climate; T · Problem-solving
resources: Personal: observation and flexible instruction. Contextual: shared materials and designated student support.
teacher_move: Use a picture check-in in SD or a private exit slip in SMP. Look for changes over time, check in privately, and follow school procedures for persistent or serious concerns. Offer a common task with an optional scaffold.
school_move: Create a shared bank of low-prep routines and agree whom to consult when a concern repeats.
check: Try one routine in one class. Note participation patterns without identifying students in this sheet.

title: Growth mindset, learning new approaches and helping peers without taking over
brite: T · Ongoing professional learning; R · Teamwork
resources: Personal: curiosity and willingness to experiment. Contextual: peer feedback, KKG or MGMP.
teacher_move: Ask permission to trade one teaching idea. Test one small change and compare one piece of student work.
school_move: Offer short reciprocal peer observation with shared planning time.
check: Agree what to keep, adjust or drop after one trial.

title: Protecting health, family and other priorities alongside meaningful teaching
resources: Personal: values and priority-setting. Contextual: reliable coverage and predictable schedules.
teacher_move: Choose one ‘rock’ from Monday’s activity and reserve time for it. Name one recurring task to simplify, move or share.
school_move: Protect planning and recovery time in the timetable and review conflicts with recurring duties.
check: At week’s end, check whether the reserved time held.

title: E1 · SD · Bu Rina
resources: Assertiveness + a school-wide parent contact norm
teacher_move: Try a reply window and ask what can be deferred before accepting a new duty.
school_move: Communicate the reply policy and rotate event roles.
ryff: Purpose and relationships are strengths. Autonomy and self-acceptance are under pressure.
prompt: What could she say when asked to take on another event?

title: E2 · SD · Pak Budi
teacher_move: Co-plan one student-led activity while sharing an established classroom routine.
school_move: Give both teachers planning time and make the pilot low-stakes.
ryff: Environmental mastery and self-acceptance are strengths. Personal growth is the tension.
prompt: What is one part of his practice worth preserving as he tries something new?

title: E3 · SD · Bu Maya
resources: Reflective habit + a supportive senior colleague and shared materials
teacher_move: Ask the mentor to model one transition and trial it with existing materials.
school_move: Schedule a weekly mentor check-in and share low-cost lesson resources.
ryff: Purpose and growth can coexist with difficulty managing daily demands.
prompt: Which difficulty needs a better routine, and which needs more support?

title: J1 · SMP · Pak Andi
brite: B · Resilience process; i · Responding to stress and work–life balance
resources: Organizational skills + leadership authority to redistribute work
teacher_move: Bring a duty snapshot and request one immediate swap or reduction.
school_move: Assign a co-lead for futsal or rotate duties and protect recovery time.
ryff: Purpose is visible. Autonomy is constrained despite effective classroom performance.
prompt: Which duty would you move first, and who can authorize it?

title: J2 · SMP · Bu Sari
brite: R · Teamwork and support networks; T · Professional learning
resources: Pedagogical confidence + MGMP and a receptive colleague
teacher_move: Invite one colleague to co-design a task with one shared learning goal.
school_move: Make space for small co-planning pilots and invite different approaches in meetings.
ryff: Autonomy and growth coexist with weaker departmental relationships.
prompt: How can she ask for collaboration while keeping room for her teaching approach?

title: J3 · SMP · Pak Hendra
brite: i · Maintaining motivation; T · Goal setting
resources: Literary interests + a colleague and protected planning time
teacher_move: Try one short poetry or creative-writing activity and reflect on whether it renewed his interest.
school_move: Give him time to pilot the activity within an existing duty.
ryff: Relationships and mastery are strengths. Purpose and growth deserve attention.
prompt: What would tell him that this is worth continuing?
